title: Structured logging with slog, zerolog and zap

videos.script: boxoffice's log lines are written for people. A program reading millions of them has to guess what each word is. {{fields}} This lesson writes them as data: one JSON object per line, every value named and typed. {{slog}} The standard library's slog does it. Levels, fields, a logger that carries a request id, and a type that hides an e-mail address by itself. {{box}} boxoffice gets a request id on every response, and one access line per request, as fields. {{others}} Then the two libraries most services used before slog. zerolog writes a line as a chain of calls. zap has a strict API and a sugared one. {{bench}} All three are measured on the same line. zerolog wins by a lot. Next to a database query, nobody would notice. {{secrets}} Last, what must never reach a log, and how to make sure it does not.
